# Mando TV

> Mando TV is a universal TV remote app for phones and computers (iPhone, iPad, Android and Windows). It controls Samsung (Tizen), LG (webOS), Roku and Google TV / Android TV televisions (Sony, Philips, TCL, Hisense, Sharp, Xiaomi, Toshiba, Panasonic, Haier, Skyworth, Chromecast with Google TV and others), plus Fire TV (Fire TV Stick, Fire TV Cube and TVs with Fire TV built in, paired with a 4-digit PIN) and Apple TV (in beta, paired with a PIN that the Apple TV shows on screen), over the home Wi-Fi network. Support for older TVs is new and in beta: LG NetCast (2011 to 2014), Vizio SmartCast (2016 and newer), Sony Bravia 2013 to 2015 without Android, Panasonic Viera (2011 to 2018) and Philips 2011 to 2015 without Android. On Android phones with an infrared blaster it can also control TVs by infrared, and on Android 9 or newer it can connect over Bluetooth, in beta. It has no ads, needs no account, and Mando TV has no servers that store what you do. The remote is free; Pro is an optional one-time purchase with no subscription.

Key facts:

- Free: remote buttons (arrows, OK, back, home, volume, channels, mute), phone keyboard to type on the TV, open TV apps, switch inputs, turn the TV on over the network, automatic TV discovery, several TVs, Easy mode with big buttons, a guest remote to share by link (for example by WhatsApp) with an expiry date of up to 31 days, infrared control on Android phones with an infrared blaster, Bluetooth on Android 9 or newer (beta), Apple TV (beta), make a Roku remote with a speaker ring so you can find it, and an in-app assistant for when the TV does not show up.
- Pro (one-time purchase, no subscription): touchpad, voice commands (on Windows they are recognized on the PC itself, with no internet), routines, sleep timer, night mode, the easy remote to share by link (up to 6 giant buttons), quick access (Android Quick Settings panel, Windows tray icon, and in beta iPhone widgets on the Home Screen and Lock Screen, Control Center buttons and Siri and Shortcuts phrases), headphone mode on LG TVs (TV sound to Bluetooth headphones), Kids mode (a remote for children with only the apps you allow and a volume cap on TVs that report their volume, optionally with a time limit after which Mando TV turns the TV off; leaving it needs your adult PIN; on some TVs children can still reach other apps from the TV's own home screen), favorite live TV channels on LG and Roku TV, sending photos and videos to LG, Samsung and Android TV / Google TV over the home Wi-Fi (not screen mirroring) and more. The exact list is on the home page of each language.
- Screen mirroring: on iPhone and iPad, Mando TV walks you to Screen Mirroring in Control Center (the iPhone's own feature, free) for TVs with AirPlay; on Windows it opens Cast (Windows + K, free). Android (Cast) gets the same shortcut with its next version. On Windows, Pro adds Mando TV's own screen mirroring over the home network to LG, Samsung, Hisense (VIDAA) and Android TV sets (beta, a few seconds of delay and no sound; for photos and presentations, not games). With Pro it can also send photos and videos to the TV.
- Connection: over Wi-Fi (phone and TV on the same network, no internet needed). Infrared is also available, only on Android phones with an infrared blaster (common on Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO), for TVs that are not smart TVs or were never connected to Wi-Fi. It is new. Bluetooth is available in beta and free on Android 9 or newer: the phone connects to the TV as a Bluetooth keyboard and remote, with no Wi-Fi needed. It works with Google TV, Android TV and Fire TV; other brands that accept Bluetooth keyboards may work; Roku does not accept them. It is not available on iPhone or Windows. Apple TV (beta, free) is controlled over the home Wi-Fi and paired with a PIN shown on the Apple TV screen; Mando TV wakes it over Wi-Fi, and with HDMI-CEC enabled in the Apple TV settings the TV turns on too.
- Platforms: App Store (iPhone and iPad), Microsoft Store (Windows) and early access on Google Play (Android).
- Languages of the website (6): Spanish, English, Portuguese, French, German and Italian.
- Languages of the app: 30 since version 1.1 (already on the App Store for iPhone and iPad and on Microsoft Store for Windows; Android gets them with its 1.1 update, until then 13): Arabic, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Slovak, Spanish, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian and Vietnamese. Voice commands (Pro) are understood in 29 of them.
- Privacy: the app controls the TV directly inside the home network, without going through the internet. The website counts visits with Cloudflare Web Analytics (no cookies) and uses Google Analytics only if the visitor accepts.
- Contact: hola@mandotv.app

## TV remote app by brand (English)

Each page says which systems that brand uses and which ones Mando TV controls (Roku TV, Google TV / Android TV, Fire TV and most Hisense VIDAA models) and which ones it does not (for example Xumo TV and Titan OS). Some recent VIDAA models only accept Hisense's official app; Mando TV detects it and says so. Vizio SmartCast TVs from 2016 onward have beta support.

- [Sony](https://mandotv.app/en/guides/sony-tv-remote-app/), [TCL](https://mandotv.app/en/guides/tcl-tv-remote-app/), [Hisense](https://mandotv.app/en/guides/hisense-tv-remote-app/), [Insignia](https://mandotv.app/en/guides/insignia-tv-remote-app/), [onn.](https://mandotv.app/en/guides/onn-tv-remote-app/), [Toshiba](https://mandotv.app/en/guides/toshiba-tv-remote-app/), [Sharp](https://mandotv.app/en/guides/sharp-tv-remote-app/), [Philips](https://mandotv.app/en/guides/philips-tv-remote-app/), [Westinghouse](https://mandotv.app/en/guides/westinghouse-tv-remote-app/), [Pioneer](https://mandotv.app/en/guides/pioneer-tv-remote-app/), [Vizio (beta support for SmartCast)](https://mandotv.app/en/guides/vizio-tv-remote-app/)
